title: Infrastructural Occupational Health and Safety
summary: Placeholder summary — replace with real description.
body: Our research and implementation initiative in Infrastructural Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) focused on integrating comprehensive risk management and hazard control across large-scale engineering and construction projects. Covering 61 districts in Bangladesh, the project strengthened institutional capacity within LGED and partner organizations, equipping field engineers, project supervisors, and consultants with essential tools to identify, monitor, and mitigate critical workplace hazards.Our team’s collective work spanned high-voltage energy transmission, road corridor logistics, heavy industrial civil works, coastal and environmental infrastructure, and rural development projects. We developed and deployed field-tested OHS controls-ranging from deep excavation protocols, fall protection, and structural safety inspections to daily toolbox meetings, labor management plans, and environmental-social compliance auditing. By advancing knowledge transfer and field-level capabilities, our initiative established lasting frameworks for climate-resilient, compliant, and safe execution across the infrastructure lifecycle.

title: Environmental & Social Safeguards Management
summary: Placeholder summary — replace with real description.
body: Our capacity development initiative in Environmental & Social Safeguards Management equipped senior public sector leadership, executive project management teams, Project Directors, Deputy Secretaries, and lead engineers across major government agencies with the knowledge and oversight tools necessary to evaluate, monitor, and govern complex Environmental and Social (ES) documentation throughout the project lifecycle. Anchored in international Environmental and Social Standards (ESS1–ESS10) and domestic statutory regulations—specifically the Bangladesh Environmental Conservation Act 1995 and Environmental Conservation Rules 2023—our team designed and coordinated a technical training curriculum that enabled high-level policy decision-makers to seamlessly embed Environmental and Social Commitment Plans (ESCP) into overarching project management models while navigating statutory compliance requirements. Furthermore, the program provided Executive and Assistant Engineers with technical methodologies to translate ESS principles into field-level contract specifications, Traffic Management Plans (ESS4), Waste and Chemical Management Plans (ESS3), and Biodiversity Mitigation Strategies (ESS6). Simultaneously, it strengthened institutional capacities among specialized directors and environment/social specialists to execute Resettlement Action Plans (ESS5), oversee Stakeholder Engagement Plans (ESS10), manage Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes (ESS7), and operationalize Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs). Finally, the initiative built targeted competencies for specialized environmental coordinators to manage multi-faceted habitat assessments (ESS6), direct long-term rehabilitation plans, and ensure financial intermediary due diligence (ESS9).
